# Decision memo: Prioritize playback reliability: high-severity failures block the core listening task

*Generated by `gpt-6-luna` (role: memo, prompt `memo-v4`) from the saved ranking and evidence pack only; all claims passed the automated check in `memo_check.json`. Human-reviewed: recommended area chosen by the project author; one sentence in Evidence added by the author and re-checked by code.*

## Recommendation

Direct next quarter’s product effort to playback reliability, especially failures that prevent a track from starting or continuing. This is a focused choice of severity per complaint and interruption of the core listening task, not the area with the largest total complaint burden. The playback issue, Music Playback Problems, has mean severity 3.65 (Claim 1), and customers describe the task failing outright: review 29162826-9af0-4a92-8bbf-ed3c269a6352 (“It won't even play my song”) and review 1ba0e0d6-5885-46e2-8754-f20e038a4951 (“the song never starts to play”). Both are typical examples, not rare worst cases. A high-severity example also reports a stereo no longer working with Spotify: review 641d2126-bc09-415d-bbfc-817a38a0b91b (“its been pulled and no longer works”).

## Evidence

Playback has 43602 complaints and severity sum 160591 in the area totals, with mean severity 3.68. Playback also has 31050 complaints at severity 4 or 5, roughly three times access (10267) and four times billing/support (7448), so it holds the largest volume of reports where a core task is blocked. In the leading issue-level evidence, playback’s 28307 complaints (Claim 2) have priority score 103197 (Claim 3) and mean severity 3.65 (Claim 1). The issue-level volume is substantial, while the severity and nature of reports make the case for tackling reliability rather than treating playback as a lower-priority polish area.

## Alternatives considered

The strongest counter-argument is billing/support: it ranks above playback in total area severity sum, with 185030 versus playback’s 160591, and has more complaints, 62732 versus 43602. Usability also has more complaints, 69060, and a higher total severity sum, 180210. Those totals matter and should not be dismissed. The trade-off is that choosing playback means not addressing the larger aggregate burdens first. I recommend it because playback reports have high severity per complaint and describe inability to perform the central listening task; volume alone would favor billing/support or usability. Billing/support’s area mean severity is 2.95 and usability’s is 2.61, compared with playback’s 3.68.

Access is a further credible alternative: its area mean severity is 3.98, above playback’s 3.68, but it has 10732 complaints and severity sum 42689, both below playback. The issue-level login mean is 3.99 (Claim 4), but access’s smaller total burden makes it a narrower next-quarter bet. This recommendation therefore accepts the risk of leaving a more severe-per-report access problem for later in favor of playback’s broader issue volume and direct task impact.

## Limitations

These are self-selected historical Google Play reviews from 17 May 2022 to 15 Nov 2023, not a representative survey or current incident measure. Cancellation language is intent, not observed churn; the pack provides no revenue data, so no revenue-at-risk or causal retention claim follows. Coverage is 660609 completed, 0 pending, and 13 quarantined out of 660622 source rows. The generic-bucket note warns that ISS-other-general is broad dissatisfaction without a specific actionable feature; it is not a suitable product-area comparator. Severity bias is material: on 50 hand-labeled golden reviews, model severity matched human labels 76% of the time and errors were almost always one level too high, so absolute severity is inflated and issue order is more reliable. Finally, independent re-labeling of 4842 sampled reviews agreed with the original on topic, intent, and severity together 78% of the time; all classifications and comparisons should be treated as directional.
